findings.title: Working-hours check rejects slots when a day has more than one working-hour range
findings.body: The new check uses `workingHours.find(...)` and returns false as soon as any range for the slot's weekday does not contain the slot. That requires the slot to fall inside every range for that day, not just one of them. Split schedules (e.g. 9–12 and 13–17) produce several ranges per day. So do schedules that cross UTC midnight, which `getWorkingHours` splits into separate ranges. In all these cases every slot fails at least one range, so valid slots are hidden for fixed and round-robin hosts. The check should pass when the slot lies within at least one range.

findings.title: Slot end is computed from the slot start time
findings.body: `end` is computed as `slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute()`, which is the same value as `start`. The test `end > workingHour.endTime` therefore never considers the event length. A slot that starts just before the end of working hours and runs past it is treated as available. It should use `slotEndTime`.

findings.title: Multiple date overrides on the same day mark every slot unavailable
findings.body: The override check also uses `dateOverrides.find(...)` and returns true (meaning unavailable) when the slot is outside any single override on that day. If a host has two override ranges on one date (e.g. 9–11 and 14–16), a slot inside the first range is outside the second, so `find` succeeds and the slot is rejected. The host ends up with no availability on that day. The slot should be accepted if it falls within any override for the date.

findings.title: Dayjs objects compared with ===, so the zero-length override check never matches
findings.body: `dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...)` compares two distinct object references, so it is always false. The intended detection of a zero-length ("unavailable all day") override never fires. Such days then go through the before/after checks, and a slot starting exactly at the override instant can be treated as available. Use `.isSame()` or compare `valueOf()`.

findings.title: Timezone-shifted override minutes wrap around midnight
findings.body: After adding the invitee/organizer offset, start and end are reduced to `hour()*60+minute()` of the shifted time. Any override that crosses midnight once shifted wraps to the wrong part of the day. Example: 17:00–20:00 UTC with a +5:30 shift becomes 22:30–01:30, giving endTime < startTime, and `buildSlots` drops the range as invalid. Shifts that push the whole range into the next or previous day are placed on the wrong day. In addition, `activeOverrides` still selects overrides by the unshifted UTC start, which is inconsistent with the shifted values. Overrides near day boundaries will show missing or incorrect slots for attendees in other timezones.

findings.title: Override day matching compares the shifted start against the slot's UTC calendar date
findings.body: An override is applied only when its shifted start formats to the same `YYYY MM DD` as `slotStartTime` in UTC. For organizers far from UTC, an override's local day spans two UTC dates. Slots on the other UTC date then neither count as part of the override nor get rejected by it. They fall through to normal working hours or busy checks, so the override is only partially enforced for fixed hosts.

findings.title: New tests do not cover the round-robin fixed-host fix or a real timezone change
findings.body: The added assertion reuses the IST day window (18:30Z boundaries) with the Dhaka timezone. It only checks that the same UTC slots come back, which does not exercise overrides shifting across day boundaries. No test covers the headline fix, a round-robin event whose fixed host has a date override. No test covers multiple overrides or working-hour ranges per day either, which is where the new checks fail.
